analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md: the date bump at line 3 and a new section at head lines 129-153, "Unregistered GLM sparse-state candidate". The base units (443-856) and the head unit (1-444) contain no other changed lines in the supplied ranges. No executable code, config, endpoints or threat-model YAML changed, so there are no concrete findings.

The new text states that `EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp` gets default-on SSD prefix-cache eligibility via `PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel`, and that `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0` opts out. It also describes a new full-state layout, `native-paged-glm5next-full-state-v1`, and `PagedImmutableSnapshot` copy-on-write ownership.

Relevant threat: T-041 (cross-tenant prefix cache, TTFT oracle, at-rest artifacts; open finding SEC-035). Its detection_hint says any change to the production gate in PrefixCachePolicy, or any widening of default-on scope, needs review. If the code that implements the GLM default-on gate is in this PR, it widens the at-rest and TTFT-oracle surface to one more model. That code, and the GLM5Next codec/store files (GLM5NextPagedSparseState.swift, Prefix/GLM5Next/, PrefixCachePolicy+Activation.swift), are not in this batch. I could not verify that the new codec keeps HMAC-only lookup tags, AAD without prompt-derived fields, cacheSalt scoping, KEK binding and the TTL/disk budget.

The doc also says GLM is outside the registered coordinator serving models. A default-on local cache for an unregistered model is therefore not covered by the routing and cacheSalt scoping story, which applies only to coordinator-authored scopes. The next pass should check the unseen code diffs against T-041 and whether the T-041 affected_files/mitigation text needs a GLM mention.
